newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end down but well above lows.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end down but well above lows.

text.p: French stocks fell on Tuesday but finished well above their session lows as reassuring U.S. economic data offset some of the nervousness triggered by a U.S. missile attack on Iraqi military targets.
Brokers said the strength of oil shares, buoyed by higher oil prices on the back of the U.S. missile raid, also helped shore up the bourse.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 5.55 points, or 0.28 percent, at 1,971.43 after coming off a low of 1,949.71. The CAC-40 September futures contract closed down four points at 1,977.
Volume was a brisk 4.11 billion francs.
A report by the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management signalled flat-to-higher economic activity in August, calming fears of an overheating U.S. economy.

The Paris bourse will be closely watching French and German economic indicators due this week -- the French second quarter GDP report will come out on Wednesday morning and economists expect to see a 0.2 percent contraction.
Investors are concerned about the French government's efforts to meet its budget goals and the criteria for European monetary union, as well as a resurgence of industrial unrest.
Among individual stocks, retailer Promodes closed up 0.49 percent at 1,224 francs after announcing the sale on Monday of its money-losing German unit Promohypermarkt.

Oil stocks rose on the back of higher oil prices and expectations of strong first-half earnings. Total closed up 1.21 percent at 384.50 francs, and Elf-Aquitaine gained 1.3 percent to finish at 381.80 francs. They both report results this week.
